transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. Um... well, I suppose I'm here because I just can’t seem to get anything in order anymore. 

It's... well, my kitchen table is just covered with things. My husband’s appointment papers, flyers from church, notes from the senior center... half-finished lists. I just... sit there looking at it all. I don't know which thing to do first, and then... the whole day is just gone.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
Um... no, I don't think so. Not depressed, really. Just... well, just frustrated with the mess, I suppose. That's all.
Have you been having trouble with your memory?
No... I don't think so. My memory seems fine. I haven't really noticed any problems with remembering things.
Do you find it hard to concentrate on one thing at a time?

Yes, I suppose so. Um... if the television is on in the next room, or... well, if two people start talking near me at the senior center, my mind just sort of follows that instead. And then I... I just lose my place in whatever I was trying to write down or plan.
Have you been worrying a lot lately?
Um... no. Not really. I don't think I worry any more than usual, I suppose. Just... everyday things.
Have these problems made it hard for you to manage everyday tasks like paying bills or keeping track of appointments?

Well... yes. I suppose. Um... sometimes bills just get left sitting under a stack of mail. And... I guess I’ve missed returning some calls. I’ve forgotten a few errands I promised my daughter I’d do... and, well, more than once I've realized too late that I never confirmed one of my husband’s appointments. So... yes, I guess it has.
Did these problems start after a stroke, head injury, or another medical illness?
Um... no. I haven't had a stroke, or... or hit my head. Nothing like that.
Have you been feeling sad much of the time?
Um... no. I don't think so. I wouldn't say I feel sad. Just... fine, mostly.
Have other people noticed problems with your memory?
Um... no. Not that I know of. No one has really... said anything to me about it.
Have you been getting lost in places that should feel familiar to you?
No... I haven't gotten lost. I know my way around just fine.
Compared with a year or two ago, do you feel less able to organize and plan things than you used to be?

Yes... I suppose so. That's... well, that's why I came in, really. I just can't seem to get anything in order anymore. My kitchen table is just... covered. It's all my husband's appointment papers, church flyers, notes from the senior center... half-finished lists. I just sit there looking at it, not knowing which thing to do first... and then the whole day is just gone.
Have you been having trouble finding the right words when you speak?
No... I don't think so. I haven't had any trouble with that.
Do you need more help than before with managing your bills?

Yes... I suppose I do. My daughter actually... she's started double-checking the bills for me. And my appointments. She just... well, she doesn't trust that I can keep it all straight on my own anymore. I even... I had to step down from leading a big event at the senior center recently. It's just... gotten to be too much.
Have you been diagnosed with any brain or neurological illness, such as Parkinson’s disease?
No... no, I haven't. Nothing like that.
Have you been diagnosed with any medical condition that began around the time these problems started?
No... I don't think so. I haven't had any new medical problems or anything like that recently. Just... just the usual aches and pains of getting older, I suppose.
Has any doctor told you that these thinking or organization problems are due to a medical condition?
No... no one has said anything like that to me.
Has your daughter said that you repeat the same questions or forget conversations?
No... she hasn't said anything like that. I don't think I do that.
Have these problems been gradually getting worse over time?
I don't... I wouldn't say they're getting worse, no. It's just... it feels like it's always been this way for me. I haven't really noticed a change.
When you were a child in school, did you already have trouble staying organized?

I suppose so, yes. Um... even when I was a little girl, my teachers would write that I was... bright, but careless. I'd forget my books, or my homework. And... well, they always had to remind me to finish my seatwork before I could go outside. So... yes.

latest_inference.note: Lifelong history since childhood of disorganization, distractibility, careless mistakes, and difficulty finishing schoolwork strongly supports ADHD and argues against late-onset mild neurocognitive disorder or cognitive disorder due to a medical condition. No evidence of neurological illness, acute medical cause, progressive decline, prominent memory loss, aphasia, or getting lost.
